GOOGL.rationale: GOOGL is a world-class franchise with accelerating revenue ($102.35B in Q3-25, +6.1% QoQ), prolific cash generation ($48.41B OCF in Q3-25), and a fortress balance sheet ($98.5B cash, D/E 38.7%). Google Cloud is growing 63% YoY with a $462B backlog, and the AI stack (Gemini, TPU, 16B tokens/min API usage) is generating real commercial returns. However, the stock has undergone a dramatic re-rating that has pushed it into extremely overvalued territory on a trailing basis: P/E has expanded 80% in twelve months (19.6x → 35.3x, 82nd percentile of its range), P/B at 11.35x (90th percentile), and earnings yield of 2.8% sits 169bp below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.49% — an unusual inversion even for premium growth names. Critically, this multiple expansion has occurred while operating margins are compressing (33.9% → 32.4% → 30.5% over three quarters), signaling negative operating leverage. The market is paying peak multiples for a business exhibiting early signs of margin deterioration. The $180-190B 2026 capex guidance and $85B equity raise further compress near-term FCF (margin dropped from 21% to 9.2% in Q1 2026) and dilute shareholders. While the qual report cites a 22.6x normalized P/E from Morningstar, this is a forward/adjusted metric distinct from the 35.3x trailing diluted P/E in the quant pack — the trailing multiple is what matters for valuation discipline. The Dow inclusion (June 29, 2026) and Berkshire's $10B participation provide structural demand support, but these are one-time flows, not fundamental catalysts that justify the valuation. A reversion to a ~28x median P/E implies ~20% downside even with flat earnings. The risk/reward skews heavily unfavorable: the business is priced for perfection while the margin trajectory is imperfect, and the earnings yield inversion against risk-free rates creates a fragile valuation regime where any earnings disappointment or rate increase triggers outsized multiple compression.
